---
title: "Database Downloads"
subtitle: Download links for the clean and merged SQLite databases
---

Each source has a **clean** database (`<source>_clean.sqlite`): the QC-passed end
product of the slim stage, with uncertain rows removed, units harmonised, and
grain-size split into its own table. The analyses on this site read these five
databases; the **merged** database combines them into one. Their table layouts are on
the [DB Schema (Clean)](./db-schema-clean.qmd) and
[DB Schema (Merged)](./db-schema-merged.qmd) pages.

## Clean databases

The clean database comes in two versions, both using the same filename
`<source>_clean.sqlite` (so keep them apart if you download both):

- **Site input** (this multised-clean v0.1.0 release): the clean database enriched
  for this site, adding `site.dist_to_aquaculture` (distance to the nearest
  Norwegian aquaculture site). This is the version the pages here read, so use these
  to reproduce the site.
- **Upstream** (the multised-slim v0.1.0 release): the base clean database as
  published by the slim pipeline, without the aquaculture distance.

Both share the same [DB Schema (Clean)](./db-schema-clean.qmd).

## Merged database

The **merged** database combines all five clean databases into one, with cross-source
duplicates removed (one row per reading). Its layout and the merge steps are on the
[DB Schema (Merged)](./db-schema-merged.qmd) page and the merged-database analyses.

| File | Download |
|:-----|:---------|
| `multised_merged.sqlite` | [Download](https://github.com/seafood-hazards/multised-clean/releases/download/v0.1.0/multised_merged.sqlite) |

: Merged database {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[45,55]"}

::: {.callout-note}
Each file is a self-contained SQLite database. To reproduce this site, use the
**site-input** clean databases (the pages read the aquaculture distance). For how the
clean databases are built from the slim stage, see the
[slim site](https://seafood-hazards.github.io/multised-slim/) under **Clean
databases**.
:::
